TWO DEFECTS FOUND IN THE PUBLISHED CHAIN, NOT PREVIOUSLY COMBINED. (1) ORBIT FACTOR IS 2x WRONG IN BOTH PROJECTIONS: finishParallel's worker() fills the dihedral image AND its colour inversion per solved rep (src/retro.zig:1426-1446, inline for 0..num_syms writing same_v[ti] and swap_v[ii]), so one solve covers 2*num_syms = 16 slots, not 8. T924's and T929's low ends both divide the slot population by num_syms only. T930 caught this at 4x3 (170276/4 = 42569 predicted vs 21578 actual reps) but applied it to T924's UNWEIGHTED mean; T929 corrected the mean but kept T924's orbit factor. Multiplying both corrections: T929's published 26.8h low end is 13.42h, and the expected 4x4 orbit-rep count is ~656,900 (floor 10367922/16 = 647995, scaled by 4x3's 1.0138 symmetry surplus). Corrected projection: 1.853e11 nodes, 13.61h serial, 1.17-2.27h at 11.64x-6x. This is BELOW 4x4.D3's 8h target and changes the go/no-go: the run is worth starting. The orbit-rep count is printed by the existing code (src/retro.zig:1560) in the first ~9 minutes, so the 8x bracket is replaced by a counted integer before any solve. (2) NODE-COUNTER SEMANTICS DIFFER BETWEEN PRODUCTION AND THE T924 PROBE: worker() accumulates out.st.nodes only inside if (solved) (src/retro.zig:1416-1418) so censored roots contribute ZERO nodes, while t924_d3_probe.zig's walkLayers adds them at the 20,000,001 cap. The two 4x3 totals (T924 183,442,515 over 20,878 sampled slots; T932 183,065,016 over 21,578 orbit reps) are 0.2% apart over different denominators and will be cross-cited as agreement if nobody says otherwise. MECHANISM FINDINGS THAT SHAPED THE SPEC: finishParallel has NO incremental flush (per-thread outputs merge only after join, src/retro.zig:1687+; checkpoint written only after it returns, 3406-3412), so kill -9/OOM/power loss destroys the whole elapsed wall, but SIGINT works (installParallelSigint 2184-2191, workers break at the top of the work loop 1370-1374, partials merge, checkpoint saves, 'INTERRUPTED - checkpoint saved. Re-run to resume'). Resume is sound and non-duplicating because worker() rebuilds its certified baseline excluding FLAG_FROM_FORWARD (1344-1349), so a resumed segment solves from the same baseline a one-shot run would use - the spec arms this as control C3, which has never been run. The censored-root CENSUS is already durable and unnoticed: worker() marks the whole orbit with FLAG_TRIED_SKIP (1452-1465) and fb/fw persist in the checkpoint, so the identity of every censored root survives on disk; T929 had to recover its stratification from a host-local transcript that was in no commit. RETRO_PARALLEL_RETRY=1 (3367-3374) already clears TRIED_SKIP for escalation at a larger budget. Uncapped is not an option: layer 0 (the empty goban) is one of the 125 censored roots per T929's per-layer distribution, and retro.zig:2195-2198 records the 2x2 empty root exceeding 4e9 nodes. Wall is LINEAR in the tail's true cost: the population-weighted censored share is (282104.8-52976.1)/20000001 = 1.1456% of reps (~7530) carrying 81% of projected nodes, so total ~= 2.55 + 11.06*X hours serial if censored reps truly cost X times the cap. Exhaustive escalation of 7530 reps at 200M would cost 110h serial, hence the spec's sampled wall-capped ladder (200 reps at 200M ~= 30min; 100 at 2G ~= 2h). Memory derived independently: total = 3^16 = 43,046,721 slots; per thread 8 B/slot ctx + 4 B/slot ThreadOut = 517 MB; 16 threads = 8.26 GB + ~0.8 GB tables ~= 9.1 GB peak, inside 4x4.D3's 32 GB budget, so memory is not why 16 threads beats 18 (that is measured: T930 11.54x vs 10.87x, T932 11.640x vs 11.416x).
